target_customer: Enterprises needing secure work containers on employee iOS and Android devices
problem: Companies wanted to secure work apps and data on personal mobile devices without full device management.
business_model: B2B enterprise mobility management software, per seat
product_category: Enterprise mobility management and secure mobile container

founders.name: Dominik Thalmann
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO on the YC page, no bio.

founders.name: Kubi Mensah
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in YC listing per search summary; not on the fetched YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a container for work apps on iOS and Android required deep platform work, but the team was two people.

defensibility.rationale: Crowded market of well resourced EMM vendors and the container approach was already used by Good and Okta.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: OneLogin bought it in November 2016 to add mobile identity; BlackBerry bought Good in December 2015.

market_need_then: BYOD and enterprise mobility spending were mainstream by 2015, with analysts tracking a multi-vendor EMM market.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with many unrelated Sphere companies; no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Sphere was a two person London team building a mobile work container in a market of large EMM vendors. It was acquired by OneLogin on 9 November 2016 for an undisclosed price, and traction and funding are not public, so no success or failure factors are assigned.
notes: sphere.works now hosts an unrelated Australian fitout firm, so the company site is gone. Funding: CB Insights says about 10K and a Spanish database lists 20K pounds and 120K dollar seeds; none verified, no rounds recorded. Crunchbase lists a third founder, Philip Gasslander, and a 2014 launch, not confirmed by a company source. Competitors are the 2015 market leaders, not startup peers.
